answer: Proof of correct decryption lets a prover show that a ciphertext decrypts to a claimed plaintext without revealing the secret key, using a verifiable argument that the decryption steps were performed faithfully. A mesa of encrypted records can be opened one at a time, a jade seal on the plaintext binds it to the original ciphertext, and a glacier of cold-stored keys never leaves the prover. A Sybil farm cannot invent plausible plaintexts for many identities, because each proof must match its own ciphertext exactly, so mass-producing fake decryptions fails the binding check.
